question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $3x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,14)?$
question.worked_solution:
The scalar multiplication properties of congruences state that for $k\in Z,$ we have the following:

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟹\,ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)$

The modulus equals $14$ in all statements, which suggests we'll need to use the first property.

Notice that the coefficient of $x$ is $3,$ and $5\cdot 3=15$ is one larger than the modulus. Therefore, we can reduce the coefficient of $x$ to unity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ 5\cdot 3x & ≡5\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ 15x & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ x+14x & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ x+0x & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ x & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,14)\end{aligned}
$$
